title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics and does not belong to the motif notes around it. It is a typed English page numbered 77, with handwritten formulas and a marginal reference 'p. 210'. In style it is a translation of a printed textbook or article on classical projective algebraic geometry; the language ('Zariski's topology', 'regular function') is that of 1950s–60s English or Russian-school texts. Its content is unrelated to the neighbouring manuscript pages on Tannakian groups of motives over F_q, Weil-number valuations and polarizations, so it is probably a misfiled sheet in cote 15.

The mathematics is the standard check that a map to projective space given by homogeneous forms is a regular morphism.
- Setup: V is a variety and f_n : V → V^(n) ⊂ P^T is defined locally by forms (φ_0^(i), …, φ_T^(i)). The superscript (i) indexes the local representations on an open cover.
- Point correspondence: the image point Q of Q' is determined by the homogeneous coordinates, or equivalently by the ratios φ_j/φ_k(Q'). Hence (φ_0^(i)(Q'), …, φ_T^(i)(Q')) = (x_0(Q), …, x_T(Q)) projectively, and Q = f_n Q'.
- Continuity and regularity: it suffices to pull back regular functions. Near Q with x_k ≠ 0, a regular function R is locally F_1(x_0/x_k, …, x_T/x_k) / F_2(x_0/x_k, …, x_T/x_k) with F_2(Q) ≠ 0. Its pullback is R' = F_1(φ/φ_k) / F_2(φ/φ_k).
- R' is regular near Q' because φ_k(Q') ≠ 0 and F_2(φ(Q')/φ_k(Q')) = F_2(Q) ≠ 0.

The argument is entirely routine. It serves a textbook construction, perhaps of a map V → V^(n) built from a linear system or from an iterated construction indexed by n.
errors: Not an error but a small gap: the text does not state that φ_k(Q') ≠ 0 must be ensured by choosing the local representation (i) suitably. That choice is implicit.
'Q ∈ V^(n) (x_k ≠ 0 at Q)' is loose phrasing for 'in a neighbourhood of Q in V^(n) where x_k ≠ 0'.
It is also only locally true that every regular function on the chart is a quotient of polynomials in the affine coordinates. This is standard and fine.

ideas.what: A map to projective space defined by forms is a regular morphism, checked by pulling back local regular functions on the affine charts x_k ≠ 0.
ideas.modern_name: Morphism to P^n defined by a linear system / sections of a line bundle; regularity criterion on affine charts
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weil, Serre FAC 1955, standard textbooks such as Shafarevich)
ideas.where_published: EGA II §4 (morphisms to projective bundles via sections of invertible sheaves), in far greater generality
